html:
SMTO-AUT-0039 — SMTO hid a reply that contained your sign-in secret

GUID: 0400fb38-ce3e-544e-a126-d32d45ee2f9a
Slug: private-http-response-withheld
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: private

What happened

  • The service answered this request, but its reply contained the secret sign-in details SMTO used, so SMTO blocked the reply instead of showing or saving it. If the request was meant to change something, it may already have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the request was meant to change something (send, create, update or delete), check on that service whether it already happened before asking again. The service received and answered the request; SMTO only hid the reply.
  2. Ask SMTO to use a different address on that service that returns the data you need, not a test or echo address that repeats your request back. Addresses that copy your sign-in token into their reply will always be blocked.
  3. To check the connection itself, open Parameter Store from the More options menu, select the saved HTTP connection, and use Test connection. The test reports whether the service is reachable and accepts your sign-in, without showing the secret.

What success looks like

  • The request returns its result normally, or Test connection shows Reachable and Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages this connection. Don't paste the token or password into a conversation to see the reply; SMTO protects it either way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • For a request made with an OAuth or private-auth HTTP connection, the binary response body, artifact or download contained private credential bytes, so the Gateway withheld it and reported auth_private_response with complete=false.

What this means

  • A protected HTTP response or artifact reflected private credential bytes, so public body/artifact publication was suppressed. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • A protected HTTP response or artifact reflected private credential bytes, so public body/artifact publication was suppressed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect public connection status and the original request's execution receipt; withholding a response does not undo a remote request.

How to fix it

  • Use the status_code and executed fields of the HTTP request result to establish whether the request took effect, then target an endpoint that does not reflect the Authorization header, token or session material (for example avoid echo, debug or token-introspection routes). Check connection health only through the saved HTTP connection's Test connection action in Parameter Store; credential reflection is suppressed regardless of redaction settings.
  • Use the authenticated connection workflow for private credentials and inspect only its public connection status.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • Public output contains no private credential material and the original operation's outcome is separately established.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
